applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where proposed mitigation trees are located adjacent to overhead electric line
findings.comment: Four mitigation trees are proposed at clearances of 0-0.8 feet from the overhead electric conductor (measured). However, species identification is missing, preventing verification of whether these are non-utility-compatible trees. Without species designation per ECM Appendix F, compliance with the 15-foot minimum clearance requirement for non-utility-compatible trees cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where proposed mitigation trees are located adjacent to overhead electric line
findings.comment: Four mitigation trees are proposed at clearances of 0-0.8 feet from the overhead electric conductor. However, species identification is missing and mature heights are not specified, preventing verification of whether any are large trees (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F). Without species and height information, compliance with the 25-foot minimum clearance requirement for large trees from distribution lines cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary at utility pole locations along overhead electric line
findings.comment: Proposed mitigation trees are positioned at measured clearances of 0-0.8 feet from overhead electric poles/conductors at the southern boundary. Minimum clearance requirement is 10 lateral feet from any electric utility pole. Three of four trees are within or directly on the utility infrastructure.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary (four mitigation trees near OHE); potentially other tree locations
findings.comment: Four proposed mitigation trees shown on the landscape plan adjacent to the overhead electric line are not identified by species. The landscape plan uses generic symbols (M for mitigation, SY for street yard, PL for parking lot) but does not label individual trees with species codes or names. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 lists shade trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm) and ornamental trees (Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) but does not clearly indicate which species are proposed at which specific locations on the landscape plan. Species identification is required to verify utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary and other areas with proposed trees near overhead electric facilities
findings.comment: Large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) cannot be differentiated from smaller trees on the landscape plan because species are not identified. Landscape plan and plant schedule lack notation indicating which proposed trees are large-stature species. Without this differentiation, the applicability of large-tree clearance restrictions (25 feet minimum from distribution conductors, 50 feet from transmission) cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where proposed trees are located adjacent to overhead electric line
findings.comment: Four proposed mitigation trees are shown on the landscape plan adjacent to the overhead electric line, but the relationship is not documented with sufficient clarity to verify compliance. Specifically: no species labels identify the trees; no dimension lines show clearance distances between tree trunks and the overhead conductor; measured clearances indicate trees are positioned at 0-0.8 feet from the OHE conductor, which appears to violate clearance requirements. The plan does not provide adequate documentation to verify clearances.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where proposed mitigation trees are located adjacent to overhead electric line
findings.comment: Four proposed mitigation trees are positioned at measured clearances of 0-0.8 feet from the overhead electric line at the southern property boundary. These clearances are within prohibited zones regardless of species (minimum 15 feet from distribution conductors for non-utility-compatible trees; minimum 25 feet for large trees; minimum 10 feet from poles). No evidence of documented written approval from Austin Energy is provided to authorize tree planting within these restricted clearance zones.

applicableAreas: Areas where underground electrical equipment is present or proposed
findings.comment: The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) identifies underground electrical equipment including transformer pads, pull boxes, and electrical meters throughout the site. However, the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show the locations of this underground equipment or clearly identify where pull boxes and transformers are positioned in relation to proposed tree locations. Without this information, clearances between proposed trees and underground equipment cannot be verified to confirm compliance with the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement.

applicableAreas: Areas where underground electrical equipment is present or proposed
findings.comment: Trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment require root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) per UCM § 1.10.10.4. However, the landscape plan does not clearly identify underground equipment locations in relation to proposed trees, and no root barrier details or specifications are shown. Without identification of trees within 20 feet of underground equipment, root barrier compliance cannot be verified.
